Ordinal 8's MIGRATION_TX and CREATOR_HISTORY both succeeded normally (candidate found, pool size 201). second_distinct_bug_found.symptom: the raw transport-level ATTEMPT_SUCCEEDED event for (8, FUNDING_TX) was already durably recorded (correctly -- the physical request genuinely succeeded at the HTTP level and correctly consumed budget) BEFORE the raise occurred. This meant succeeded_stage_keys() already included (8, FUNDING_TX), and stage_output_ledger.record_stage_output() was NEVER reached (the raise happens before that line) -- so ordinal 8 had NO stage output at all.
second_distinct_bug_found.risk: _member_has_failed_stage(8) returned None (not blocked) and _stage_for_next(8) returned None (looked fully complete) purely because of the raw ATTEMPT_SUCCEEDED event -- a future resume_next() call would have SILENTLY SKIPPED ordinal 8 and moved to ordinal 9, permanently losing the fact that raw evidence contradicted the local prediction. This is an evidence-loss risk, more serious than the earlier B2Z-P2D liveness bug (which was merely stuck, not silently wrong).
second_distinct_bug_found.distinguishing_feature_from_p2d: B2Z-P2D's NO_CANDIDATE_TERMINAL fix addressed a member that made ZERO progress (safe but stuck forever). This bug is the opposite failure mode: the member LOOKED complete and would have been silently treated as resolved with no evidence, which is worse because it could pass unnoticed.

fix.member_now_correctly_blocks: _member_has_failed_stage() was updated to treat (ordinal, FUNDING_TX) as NOT succeeded when a SEMANTIC_VALIDATION_FAILED_TERMINAL exists for that ordinal, even though a raw ATTEMPT_SUCCEEDED event also exists -- so the member now correctly BLOCKS resume (exactly like an unexcluded ATTEMPT_FAILED_AFTER_DISPATCH would), requiring an explicit human decision to skip past it, rather than being silently bypassed
fix.cannot_be_excluded_via_the_wrong_mechani: exclude_member_from_execution() (the B2Z-P2R credential-corruption exclusion path) was verified to correctly REJECT an attempt to exclude a SEMANTIC_VALIDATION_FAILED_TERMINAL member -- it only matches ATTEMPT_FAILED_AFTER_DISPATCH, so a genuine local-vs-raw disagreement cannot be swept aside using the mechanism meant only for credential/infrastructure corruption. A distinct, explicit decision path would be needed if a human later decides ordinal 8 should be skipped.
